prompt: How much discount did each extra unit cost? For each promotion that started in 2025 (start_date from 1 January to 31 December 2025), give discount_eur, the line_discount_eur summed over the lines that carry it; extra_units, its units on promotion minus its baseline units; and discount_per_extra_unit, discount_eur divided by extra_units, rounded to 2 decimals with ROUND, or missing when extra_units is 0 or less. A sales line is on a promotion when it carries that promotion's ID in order_lines.promo_id, whatever its date; where two promotions overlap on a product, a line carries only the deeper one, so it counts once. The baseline ends the day before the promotion's start_date and has as many days as the promotion ran, start_date and end_date both counted; it holds every sales line of the promotion's products in those days, whatever promotion the line carries. Days are sales.order_date, the UTC day of the order. A period with no sale counts 0. A promotion with no line on it has a discount_eur of 0 and extra_units of 0 or less, so its discount_per_extra_unit is missing. A missing line_discount_eur counts as 0; a discount_eur of 0 with extra_units above 0 gives a discount_per_extra_unit of 0. Return four columns, in this order: promo_id, discount_eur, extra_units and discount_per_extra_unit. Return one row for each such promotion. Any row order is fine.
hints: Next, add up the discount and the units on promotion, then subtract the baseline units to get the extra units.
Divide only when the extra units are above 0; a CASE with no ELSE leaves the other rows missing.
why_this_works: The discount comes from the lines that carry the promotion and the extra units from a same-length baseline, so their ratio prices each extra unit.
